task.name: `forge diagnose` resolves another repository's issue references against the local repo and injects the results as starting evidence
task.story_text:
## Observed behavior

`forge diagnose` pre-loads "starting evidence" from references it finds in the
issue body, and resolves bare `#NNNN` references against the repository it is
running in — even when the issue is about a different project. The agent is then
handed unrelated content presented as evidence for the bug under investigation.

Issue #2029 describes a failure observed in the adopter project `hdp` and refers
to that project's stories as `#246`, `#248`, `#245` and `#231`. Diagnose run
`59bdfe42256b`, executed in the `theforge` checkout, reported:

```
[diagnose] pre-loaded 2 evidence excerpt(s) from issue-body references: PR #246, PR #248
```

Those are `theforge` pull requests from April 2026:

```
PR #246  MERGED 2026-04-01  Soft conventions — prompt-injected project standards
                            for plan/dev/review
PR #248  MERGED 2026-04-01  Story source abstraction — specs from GitHub issues,
                            local files, or external trackers
```

The issue's actual referents:

```
hdp #246  Native session state is lost on app relaunch: false end-of-session
          error and 24h start block
hdp #248  Watch rest alarm follow-up: dismiss, re-anchor, and zero-time
          scheduling defects
```

Two merged pull requests about prompt conventions and story sources were
injected into the prompt under the heading `== STARTING EVIDENCE (auto-loaded
from issue body references) ==` for an investigation into a sandbox capability
gap. This is the only automatic evidence-gathering step in the diagnose flow,
and on a cross-project issue it is the step most likely to be wrong.

## Expected behavior

Evidence presented to an investigating agent as evidence must be evidence. A
reference resolved against the wrong subject is not a harmless miss — it is
asserted context that the agent has been told is relevant, and an investigation
that reasons from it reaches a conclusion the operator has no way to attribute
to the substitution. Where a reference cannot be resolved against the subject it
was written about, loading nothing is correct and loading something else is not;
a best-effort mechanism whose failure mode is confidently wrong content is not
best-effort. More generally, a reference is only meaningful relative to the
namespace it was written in, so a mechanism that resolves references must either
establish that namespace or decline to resolve, rather than defaulting to
whichever namespace it happens to be executing in.

## Diagnosis

- **Observed symptom:** bare `#NNNN` references in an issue body that describe
  another repository's issues are resolved against the local repository, and the
  unrelated results are injected into the diagnose prompt as starting evidence.

- **Evidence:** the extraction pattern is namespace-free —
  `_ISSUE_PR_RE = re.compile(r"#(\d{1,7})\b")` at
  `src/theforge/coordinator/diagnose_evidence.py:64` — so it captures a number
  with no owner or repository qualifier and no record of where the reference was
  written. Resolution then binds those numbers to the local repository:
  `_load_pr_issue_refs` (`diagnose_evidence.py:323-364`) calls `gh pr view <n>`
  and falls back to `gh issue view <n>`, and `_run_gh`
  (`diagnose_evidence.py:272-286`) executes with `cwd=str(project_root)`
  (line 279), which makes `gh` resolve against the checkout's own remote. Both
  loaders fail open on error but succeed on a wrong-repository hit, so a number
  that happens to exist locally always resolves and always resolves incorrectly.
  Observed end to end in run `59bdfe42256b`, whose audit records
  `starting_evidence: {reference_labels: ['PR #246', 'PR #248'], chars: 560}` for
  an issue whose `#246`/`#248` denote `hdp` issues.

- **Ruled out:** not a `gh` misconfiguration — both lookups returned the correct
  `theforge` PRs for the numbers they were given; the defect is in which
  repository the numbers were sent to, not in the lookup. Not a body-parsing
  error — the issue body does state `#246`/`#248` literally, and the pattern
  matched what was written. Not confined to the `#NNNN` loader — the same
  local-root assumption governs the other reference kinds, since `_HEX_ID_RE`
  run and sprint ids are probed under `project_root / ".forge"`
  (`diagnose_evidence.py:143-191`) and `_load_branch_history`
  (`diagnose_evidence.py:289-320`) shares `_run_gh`; the `#NNNN` case is simply
  the one that silently succeeds instead of finding nothing.

- **Confirmed cause:** the reference extractor captures no namespace and the
  loaders bind every reference to the local project root, so an issue written
  about another repository resolves its references against this one. There is no
  representation of the subject repository anywhere in the evidence path, so the
  mechanism cannot distinguish a correct hit from a collision on the same number.

- **Affected code path:** `src/theforge/coordinator/diagnose_evidence.py` —
  `_ISSUE_PR_RE` (line 64), `_load_pr_issue_refs` (lines 323-364), `_run_gh`
  (lines 272-286), and `build_starting_evidence` (lines 370-405) which assembles
  the block; consumed by
  `src/theforge/task/diagnose_prompts.py:203-237` (`build_diagnose_prompt`).

- **Fix-success criterion:** diagnosing an issue whose body references another
  repository's issues by bare number loads no excerpt for those references, or
  loads the correct excerpt from the repository they were written about; in
  neither case does the rendered starting-evidence block contain content from a
  same-numbered issue or pull request in the local repository.

## Notes

This is one half of a broader limit: `forge diagnose` reads one repository, and
an issue filed in `theforge` about behavior observed in an adopter cannot reach
that adopter's run artifacts at all. That limit is real and is not what this
issue asks to fix — an investigation that correctly reports it has no evidence is
sound, and the diagnose agent does report it. What this issue asks is that the
mechanism stop substituting wrong evidence for absent evidence, which is a
strictly worse failure than the limit itself.

Found while testing whether `forge diagnose` can produce a runbook-grade
Diagnosis section without operator-supplied evidence.

handoff.summary: Made forge diagnose's starting-evidence pre-load namespace-aware. Bare #NNNN references in an issue body are no longer resolved against the repository diagnose happens to be executing in; only repository-qualified references (owner/repo#NNNN and github.com issue/PR URLs) are resolved, and each lookup is pinned to the repository it names with `gh --repo`. Extraction now uses _QUALIFIED_REF_RE and _GITHUB_URL_REF_RE via a new _extract_qualified_refs helper, which also rejects conventional-commit branch heads (feat/issue-2057#3) that are shaped like owner/repo#NNNN. Bare numbers are still detected but only so they can be reported as deliberately declined: StartingEvidence gains declined_labels, DiagnoseState gains starting_evidence_declined, the diagnose flow emits a decline line, and the audit records starting_evidence.declined_unqualified_refs — so an operator sees 'declined on purpose' rather than inferring silence from an empty block.

commits.message: fix(diagnose): resolve issue-body references only in the namespace they name

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Diagnosing an issue whose body references another repository's issues by bare number loads no excerpt for those references, or loads the correct excerpt from the repository they were written about; in neither case does the rendered starting-evidence block contain content from a same-numbered issue or pull request in the local repository.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Bare #NNNN fires zero gh lookups (TestUnqualifiedReferencesAreNotResolved::test_bare_number_fires_no_gh_lookup reproduces the #2029 body — #246/#248/#245/#231 — with a stub that would return local PR content, and asserts calls == [] and an empty block). Qualified references resolve against the repo they name via `gh pr view N --repo owner/repo` / `gh issue view N --repo owner/repo`, covered by test_qualified_ref_loads_view_pinned_to_its_repo and test_github_url_reference_is_resolved_against_its_repo.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A mechanism that resolves references must either establish that namespace or decline to resolve, rather than defaulting to whichever namespace it happens to be executing in.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Establishment is by written form only: owner/repo#NNNN or a github.com URL. Anything else declines. Ambiguous tokens (branch-prefix heads) decline rather than guess. project_root is retained as the gh subprocess cwd for auth/config resolution but no longer determines which repository a number denotes.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Best-effort/bounded design constraints of the module are preserved.
acceptance_criteria.notes: _MAX_GH_ATTEMPTS_PER_KIND still bounds attempts (test_many_unresolved_refs_are_gh_call_bounded, rewritten to use qualified refs), gh failures still fail open (test_gh_failure_fails_open), and the total char cap is unchanged.

story_deviations: Modified four tests in tests/test_diagnose_evidence.py (test_pr_number_loads_view_and_skips_self_issue -> test_qualified_ref_loads_view_pinned_to_its_repo, test_gh_failure_fails_open, test_many_unresolved_refs_are_gh_call_bounded). These encoded bare-#NNNN local resolution, which is the defect under repair, so they could not survive the fix unchanged; each was rewritten to the qualified form rather than weakened. No unrelated test files were touched.

Added declined-reference reporting (StartingEvidence.declined_labels, DiagnoseState.starting_evidence_declined, a diagnose emit line, and an audit field) beyond the literal fix-success criterion. Rationale: the fix converts a loudly-wrong behavior into a silent no-op, and convention 6 requires cross-phase data be visible in the audit trail. Small and additive; flagging in case the reviewer considers it out of scope.

The self-issue skip in _load_pr_issue_refs still matches on number alone, not (repo, number). A cross-repo reference whose number coincides with the issue under diagnosis is therefore skipped rather than loaded. This errs toward loading nothing — the safe direction per the spec — and avoids an extra `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner` subprocess to learn the local slug. Documented in the function docstring.
deferred_items: Deliberate behavior loss, not a defect: a bare #NNNN that genuinely denotes a local issue no longer pre-loads. GitHub's own rendering treats it as local, but it is mechanically indistinguishable from the cross-project case, and the fix-success criterion is unconditional. Operators wanting the preload should write owner/repo#NNNN.

The hex-id, .forge/ path, and branch loaders still bind to the local project root, as the spec's 'Ruled out' section notes. Left unchanged: they fail open to nothing rather than succeeding wrongly, so they do not exhibit the substitution failure this issue targets.

Full-suite run: 6597 passed, 17 failed. All 17 are in tests/test_cut_rc_isolation.py, tests/test_sprint_lock.py, and tests/test_sprint_reexec_collision.py, failing on `mktemp: mkstemp failed ... Operation not permitted` — sandbox-restricted temp/subprocess operations in files this change does not touch or import. Not verified against a clean baseline: a `git stash` comparison conflicted on the untracked .forge/handoff.yaml and was abandoned after confirming the working tree was intact. The coordinator's out-of-sandbox gate should clear these; if it does not, they warrant separate investigation.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules
Keep modules single-purpose; extract instead of growing monolith files
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
